ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the side DC of the rectangle ABCD is on the x-axis, and point B is on the graph of the hyperbola \(y=\frac{3}{x}\). Point E is the trisection point of side AD closer to point A. Connect CE and extend it to intersect the y-axis at point F. What is the area of \(\triangle CDF\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the lengths of the rectangle's sides be AB=CD=a, AD=BC=b,\\
since point B is on the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{3}{x}$,\\
therefore B$\left(\frac{3}{b}, b\right)$,\\
therefore OC=$\frac{3}{b}$,\\
since point E is the trisection point on side AD closer to point A,\\
therefore DE=$\frac{2}{3}b$,\\
since AD$\parallel$y-axis,\\
therefore $\triangle FOC\sim \triangle EDC$,\\
therefore $\frac{OF}{ED}=\frac{OC}{CD}$, that is, $\frac{OF}{\frac{2}{3}b}=\frac{\frac{3}{b}}{a}$,\\
therefore OF=$\frac{2}{a}$,\\
therefore the area $S_{\triangle CDF}=\frac{1}{2}CD\cdot OF=\frac{1}{2}a\cdot\frac{2}{a}=\boxed{1}$

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the lengths of the rectangle's sides be AB=CD=a, AD=BC=b,\\
since point B is on the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{3}{x}$,\\
therefore B$\left(\frac{3}{b}, b\right)$,\\
therefore OC=$\frac{3}{b}$,\\
since point E is the trisection point on side AD closer to point A,\\
therefore DE=$\frac{2}{3}b$,\\
since AD$\parallel$y-axis,\\
therefore $\triangle FOC\sim \triangle EDC$,\\
therefore $\frac{OF}{ED}=\frac{OC}{CD}$, that is, $\frac{OF}{\frac{2}{3}b}=\frac{\frac{3}{b}}{a}$,\\
therefore OF=$\frac{2}{a}$,\\
therefore the area $S_{\triangle CDF}=\frac{1}{2}CD\cdot OF=\frac{1}{2}a\cdot\frac{2}{a}=\boxed{1}$

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows rectangle ABCD with DC horizontal on the x-axis. A and D are on the left vertical side, B and C on the right vertical side, and B lies on the hyperbola y=3/x. Point E is on AD, closer to A, and segment CE is drawn and extended to meet the y-axis at F. Reasoning: Let C=(c,0), D=(c-a,0), B=(c,b), A=(c-a,b), where CD=a and BC=b. Since B is on y=3/x, we have b=3/c, so cb=3. Since E is the trisection point of AD closer to A, its height above the x-axis is 2b/3, so E=(c-a,2b/3). The slope of CE is ((2b/3)-0)/((c-a)-c)=-2b/(3a). Using point C, the line CE has y=(-2b/(3a))(x-c). At the y-axis, x=0, so the y-coordinate of F is OF=2bc/(3a)=2/a because bc=3. Triangle CDF has base CD=a on the x-axis and height OF=2/a. Therefore its area is (1/2)*a*(2/a)=1.
